task1.prompt: The line graph illustrates the percentage of internet users across three age categories (18-25, 26-50, 51+) in the UK from 2010 to 2025.

Qisqa namuna: 140 so'z. Imtihonda kamida 150 so'z yozish kerak.

The provided line graph delineates the trajectory of internet adoption among three distinct British demographics over a fifteen-year period spanning from 2010 to 2025.

Overall, it is readily apparent that internet usage escalated across all three age cohorts, with the youngest demographic maintaining an uninterrupted preeminence throughout the surveyed timeframe, while the senior group exhibited the most pronounced relative acceleration.

Commencing in 2010, approximately 78% of youths aged 18 to 25 utilized the internet, a figure that climbed steadily to reach complete saturation at 99% by 2025. Similarly, individuals aged 26 to 50 displayed consistent growth, ascending from 55% to 88%.

task2.title: AI & Automation in the Modern Workforce
task2.prompt: Artificial intelligence and autonomous robotics are developing at a pace that could eliminate millions of jobs. Some believe governments should impose heavy taxes on automation to protect human employment. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

G'oyalar: Advantages: Speed, reduction in armed bank robberies, automated accounting. Disadvantages: Cybersecurity failures during blackouts, exclusion of elderly and homeless citizens.

task2.title: Youth Crime: Retributive Imprisonment vs Community Rehabilitation
task2.prompt: Some believe that juvenile offenders should receive identical custodial prison sentences as adults to deter crime, while others argue that rehabilitation and education are more effective. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
task2.guide:
Pozitsiya: Rehabilitation, counseling, and vocational schooling prevent recidivism far better than punitive adult incarceration.

G'oyalar: Imprisoning teens with seasoned adult criminals hardens antisocial tendencies and creates career convicts. Community mentoring addresses root causes like trauma and poverty.

Reja: Intro -> Body 1 (Argument for harsh custodial deterrence) -> Body 2 (The overwhelming efficacy of educational rehabilitation and psychological counseling) -> Opinion & Conclusion.

Foydali iboralar: juvenile offender, recidivism rate, custodial sentencing, restorative justice, rehabilitative intervention

task2.title: Meat Consumption and Global Greenhouse Gas Emissions
task2.prompt: To combat global warming and environmental degradation, people should significantly reduce their consumption of meat and animal products. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
task2.guide:
Pozitsiya: Strongly Agree: Industrial livestock farming generates massive methane emissions, deforestation, and water waste compared to plant-based agriculture.

G'oyalar: Cattle generate methane, a greenhouse gas 28x more potent than CO2. Clearing the Amazon for soy animal feed destroys carbon sinks. Shifting to plant protein feeds more people using 75% less land.

Reja: Intro -> Body 1 (Environmental destructiveness of beef production: methane and land clearing) -> Body 2 (Nutritional viability and ecological savings of plant-centric diets) -> Conclusion.

Foydali iboralar: industrial livestock farming, methane emission, deforestation footprint, plant-based protein transition, land-use efficiency

task2.title: Mandatory Retirement Ages vs Working in Senior Years
task2.prompt: Some argue that employees should be forced to retire at age 65 to make room for younger generations, while others contend that workers should be permitted to continue working as long as they are competent. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
task2.guide:
Pozitsiya: Workers should be evaluated on competence rather than arbitrary chronological age, ensuring seasoned mentorship without blocking youth.

G'oyalar: Forced retirement deprives companies of institutional memory and damages senior mental health. However, progressive phased-retirement models allow seniors to mentor younger successors.

Reja: Intro -> Body 1 (Arguments for mandatory retirement: opening promotional ladders for youth) -> Body 2 (Arguments for voluntary continuation: intellectual capability, economic independence) -> Opinion (Phased mentoring roles) -> Conclusion.

Foydali iboralar: mandatory retirement threshold, institutional wisdom, chronological age discrimination, phased retirement, generational succession

task2.title: International Aid: Financial Donations vs Technological and Educational Transfer
task2.prompt: Rich nations should provide aid to developing countries through direct monetary grants, while others argue that transferring technology, clean energy, and educational infrastructure is far more effective. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
task2.guide:
Pozitsiya: Direct monetary aid frequently fuels corruption; technological and infrastructural partnerships cultivate sustainable, self-sufficient economic autonomy.

G'oyalar: Cash aid easily vanishes into bureaucratic embezzlement and creates debt traps. Transferring renewable energy grids, agricultural machinery, and universities builds permanent self-reliance.

Reja: Intro -> Body 1 (Benefits and pitfalls of direct financial donations) -> Body 2 (Superior long-term advantages of knowledge and technological capacity building) -> Opinion & Conclusion.

Foydali iboralar: sustainable autonomy, bureaucratic embezzlement, dependency syndrome, technology transfer, infrastructure endowment

task2.title: Standardized Testing in School Admissions
task2.prompt: Standardized tests such as the SAT and national university entrance exams are widely used to assess students for university admissions. Do the advantages of standardized testing outweigh its disadvantages?
task2.guide:
Pozitsiya: Advantages outweigh disadvantages when complemented by holistic reviews: standardized tests provide an objective, merit-based metric across diverse high schools.

G'oyalar: Criticisms: High-income students can afford expensive private tutoring. Strengths: Eliminates grade inflation in schools and enables gifted students from rural or underprivileged backgrounds to prove academic merit objectively.

Reja: Intro (Advantages outweigh disadvantages with holistic context) -> Body 1 (Disadvantages: commercial test prep advantages, test anxiety) -> Body 2 (Decisive advantages: combating corrupt grading, nationwide equal-footing standard) -> Conclusion.

Foydali iboralar: standardized metric, merit-based evaluation, grade inflation, socioeconomic disparity, objective academic benchmark

task2.title: Some people believe that artificial intelligence will replace teachers
task2.prompt: Some people believe that artificial intelligence will replace teachers in the future, while others think teachers will always remain essential. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
task2.guide:
Qisqa namuna: 179 so'z. Imtihonda kamida 250 so'z yozish kerak.

The inexorable proliferation of artificial intelligence has ignited impassioned debate regarding the future viability of the pedagogical profession. While techno-optimists contend that algorithmic tutoring systems will inevitably render human educators obsolete, I firmly align with the conviction that human teachers embody irreplaceable pedagogical and empathetic dimensions that technology cannot replicate.

On one hand, advocates of automated education emphasize that AI engines can personalize curricular pacing with unprecedented precision. Machine learning models analyze student diagnostic telemetry instantaneously, adapting practice modules to redress granular cognitive deficiencies. Furthermore, scalable digital tutors can democratize world-class instructional materials across socioeconomically underserved regions.

Nevertheless, teaching transcends mere cognitive data dissemination. Education is fundamentally a relational endeavor predicated on psychological mentoring, moral guidance, and affective attunement. A human teacher discerns nuanced emotional cues—frustration, despondency, or nascent curiosity—and modulates motivational strategies accordingly. Moreover, the cultivation of critical thinking, collaborative inquiry, and ethical discernment requires interactive classroom discourse that no algorithm can orchestrate.

In conclusion, while artificial intelligence will undeniably serve as an indispensable auxiliary teaching assistant, the profound holistic mentorship of human teachers ensures their enduring indispensability.

task2.title: Governments should place heavy taxes on polluting companies rather tha
task2.prompt: Governments should place heavy taxes on polluting companies rather than subsidizing clean energy. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
task2.guide:
Qisqa namuna: 169 so'z. Imtihonda kamida 250 so'z yozish kerak.

The optimal fiscal framework for combating anthropogenic climate degradation remains a contentious policy quandary. While punitive environmental taxation compels corporate accountability under the polluter-pays principle, I contend that an asymmetric reliance on taxation is suboptimal, and that strategic public subsidization of decarbonization infrastructure remains equally essential.

Punitive environmental levies undeniably yield immediate economic deterrence. By internalizing negative environmental externalities, carbon taxation renders carbon-intensive industrial methodologies economically unviable, incentivizing corporate executives to eliminate emissions or face crippling financial liability. Furthermore, tax revenues generated can finance regional ecological restoration.

However, penalizing pollution without providing economically viable technological alternatives risks crippling foundational industrial supply chains. Renewable energy technologies—such as grid-scale battery storage and green hydrogen electrolyzers—entail formidable upfront capital expenditure and extended amortization periods. Without targeted governmental subsidies, private enterprise cannot overcome initial capital hurdles.

In conclusion, fiscal environmental policy must not function as a blunt binary choice. True ecological transition necessitates a balanced dual framework: rigorous environmental taxation to disincentivize polluters, coupled with robust clean energy subsidies to accelerate technological deployment.
